verdict.reason: The tests verify mismatches in declaration, HEAD, baseline, implementation fingerprint, resolution fingerprint, profile, worktree cleanliness, and authority readability, but they do not vary the resolved Cargo target directory, crate, feature set, or expected rustdoc JSON path. Thus they do not verify the anchor’s central requirement that reuse is rejected unless every listed execution-identity component matches.

The test verifies fail-closed handling only for malformed JSON parsing. It does not verify load_from_path’s entry-relevant fingerprinting of the immutable baseline bytes or that reuse is bound to the required complete identity.

The test only verifies that malformed baseline JSON yields ParseFailed. It does not verify the entry-relevant cited promise concerning authoritative-input-set enforcement, prohibited external inputs, architecture-rules-based baseline discovery, or fail-closed handling without partial fingerprints or fallback.

The test only verifies that malformed baseline JSON produces ParseFailed. It does not exercise the load_from_path-related portion of the promise—preventing reuse of an old result or snapshot when baseline content/decoding cannot be established—and does not verify any promised reuse or fingerprint gate.

The test only verifies that malformed JSON returns ParseFailed; it does not verify load_from_path’s entry-relevant promise of fixing the resolved input as an immutable content-addressed snapshot from the same bytes.

The test only verifies that malformed JSON yields ParseFailed. It does not verify the load_from_path-relevant promise that resolved bytes are frozen as a content-addressed in-memory snapshot (including hashing and typed decoding of the same immutable bytes).

The test only verifies that malformed JSON produces ParseFailed. It does not verify load_from_path's entry-relevant obligation to operate on one immutable content snapshot, including protection against path re-read/ABA changes while hashing and decoding.

The tests verify crate-name identity, selected-feature forwarding, a decoded rustdoc format, hash presence, and several failure paths, but they never verify that the fingerprint binds declaration, resolution set, Rust implementation, Cargo execution conditions, and expected rustdoc output as one complete identity, nor that input-finalization or fingerprint-construction failure is fail-closed.

The tests verify capture construction, exporter failure propagation, and several symlink guards, but never exercise or inspect the implementation fingerprint: they do not verify that it is derived only from D3 authoritative inputs, excludes forbidden directories, rejects unrepresentable external inputs, follows architecture-rules.json discovery, or avoids partial/fallback fingerprints on limits, I/O errors, or concurrent mutation.

The tests verify basic snapshot construction, feature forwarding/export failure, and symlink guards, but never exercise type-signal result reuse, the full cache-key equality conditions, clean-worktree gating, authoritative implementation-input fingerprinting, or rejection without fallback when authoritative inputs cannot be completely identified or fingerprinted.

Bound tests verify successful capture, exporter-failure propagation, and symlink guards, but do not exercise exclusive-lock serialization, the 120-second acquisition limit, or fail-closed behavior on lock acquisition/operation failure without lockless export, existing-JSON reuse, or retry.

The tests verify symlink rejection for workspace roots and configured target-directory components, but do not verify the anchor's central capture_current guarantee: serialization under one exclusive lock with a 120-second limit, exclusive ownership of a dedicated target directory, and enforcement that every writer uses the same lock and ownership boundary.

The tests never simulate lock-acquisition timeout or lock-operation failure and do not verify fail-closed termination, absence of lockless export or existing-JSON reuse, or absence of retry after 120 seconds.

The tests verify fail-closed rejection of symlinked workspace/target paths, but do not verify that capture_current handles the shared rustdoc output lock only on Unix using descriptor-relative, no-follow trusted-root validation, nor that unsupported platforms or otherwise unverifiable target directories are rejected.

The tests verify rejection of symlinked workspace/target paths, but do not verify the central capture_current restriction that export proceeds only on Unix when a descriptor-relative, no-follow trusted-root lock is actually available, nor fail-closed rejection for unsupported platforms or an otherwise unverifiable trusted root.

The tests verify successful capture, identity/data/hash construction, exporter error propagation, and symlink rejection, but they never exercise or demonstrate that one lock remains held continuously across expected-output-path selection, export, output-path validation, and JSON-byte reading, nor that generation mixing or ABA replacement is rejected fail-closed.

The tests assert successful decoding/hash shape, feature forwarding, exporter-error propagation, and symlink rejection, but they do not verify that the expected-path check and JSON-byte snapshot read occur within the same lock interval, that target ownership and participation of all writers in that lock are established before treating output as authoritative, or that the starting snapshot fingerprint is revalidated before publishing the result.

The tests cover basic capture, exporter-error propagation, and symlink rejection, but never exercise the target-directory lock across export/check/read, rejection of undetectable non-cooperating writers, or invalidation when either fingerprint changes after capture begins. Thus the anchor's central concurrency and immutable-snapshot guarantees remain unverified for capture_current.

The bound tests do not exercise lock acquisition, same-target-directory serialization, the 120-second limit, or fail-closed behavior after a lock failure; they therefore leave the cited anchor's central lock guarantee unverified.

The tests verify rejection of symlinked workspace/target paths, including an absolute target with a symlinked ancestor, but they do not verify the anchor’s central entry-relevant guarantee: that all exports/writers for the same resolved Cargo target directory are serialized by one exclusive lock with a 120-second limit and that non-exclusive or non-cooperative target directories fail closed.
The tests do not simulate shared-output-lock acquisition failure or the 120-second timeout, and they do not verify fail-closed termination without lockless export, existing-JSON reuse, or retry.

The tests verify fail-closed rejection of symlinked workspace/target paths, but do not verify that the shared rustdoc-output lock is available only on Unix or that unsupported platforms and otherwise unverifiable target directories are rejected fail-closed.

The tests verify fail-closed rejection for several symlinked or out-of-root paths, but do not verify the central platform/lock restriction: export and snapshot reuse must be allowed only on Unix when descriptor-relative, no-follow trusted-root locking is available, and rejected on non-Unix or when that locking capability is unavailable.

The tests verify successful capture, decoding, hashing, and several symlink guards, but never exercise or observe that one lock is held continuously across expected-output-path resolution, export, output-path verification, and JSON-byte snapshot reading, nor that generation mixing or ABA is rejected fail-closed.

The tests exercise successful capture, hashing, path trust, and symlink rejection, but never verify the anchor’s central concurrency guarantees: that expected-path validation and byte snapshotting occur within the same lock, that output is rejected when exclusive target ownership/all-writer lock participation is unconfirmed, or that the starting snapshot fingerprint is rechecked before returning the result.

The tests exercise decoding/error mapping, trusted-root and symlink rejection, exporter failure, and basic snapshot construction, but never verify exclusive target-directory locking across export through output verification/read, rejection of undetectable non-cooperating writers, or failure when input/resolution fingerprints change without path-reread or ABA acceptance.
